methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
Redwood Materials is a Series D climate and energy company founded by J. B. Straubel, currently valued at $6.0B post-money following $2.125B in cumulative capital raised. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of nine climate-tech companies—one public (Lenz Energy, LNZA) and eight private firms including KoBold Metals, QuantumScape, Helion, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method applies a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier from the Series D post-money valuation of $6.0B, implying $9.0B at the next funding stage. The peer-median approach across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. This wide spread reflects heterogeneous company maturity and technology risk within the cohort.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $850M (low) to $10.3B (high), with a median estimate of $5.0B. The current $6.0B valuation sits above the median, reflecting stage advancement and capital efficiency relative to peers. Key uncertainties include technology commercialization timelines, commodity price exposure, and the applicability of earlier-stage peer multiples to a maturing Series D company with substantial capital deployment ahead.
